subject.title: feat: validate required run artifacts against a schema (`--require-artifact-schema`)

question: Should Crabbox own `--require-artifact-schema` as a public validation feature, and if so should it use this bespoke fail-closed subset or a maintained standards-compatible validator?
rationale: The current patch is technically credible, but choosing the permanent schema language, dependency policy, and SSH-only initial scope is product ownership rather than a mechanical correctness decision.

options.title: Use maintained validation
options.body: Keep the additive gate but replace the bespoke dialect with a maintained standards-compatible validator and focused CLI compatibility tests.

options.title: Accept the bespoke subset
options.body: Land the current fail-closed subset and explicitly own its documented keyword set, error behavior, and future compatibility.

options.title: Keep validation repo-owned
options.body: Do not add the flag and continue requiring each repository command to validate its own evidence before Crabbox checks artifact existence.

recommendation.title: Use maintained validation
recommendation.body: Keep the additive gate but replace the bespoke dialect with a maintained standards-compatible validator and focused CLI compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They performed the latest correctness passes and explicitly identified this exact unresolved contract choice.
